answer: Reputation-weighted escrow routing. Each identity must hold a small, non-transferable escrow that grows with its verified task history; a fresh clone starts at zero and can only bid on low-value jobs. The orchard of established agents routes high-value work only to escrowed peers, so cloning yields no access to profitable tasks. An attacker pays the escrow plus the cost of building history for every clone, while an honest agent pays once and compounds it. A basalt ledger anchors escrow state against rollback, and a lotus-style slow-release refund deters exit-and-reclone.
